lesson: The slab is the first prefab assembly on site: everything that lands on it (plates, posts, drains, water service) is already known from the panels and fixtures, so the slab layout is derived, not drawn.
rule: 1) Take the slab edge from the framing outer faces and the anchor lines from the bottom-plate segments of the current wall panels; at door openings there is no plate and no anchor. 2) Place anchors per plate segment: max spacing and end distance from the engineer (assumed 1219 / 305 mm), at least two per segment, clear of stud axes. 3) Keep stub-ups out of the thickened edge and record them from one slab corner. 4) A curbless shower is a slab recess with the full slab thickness below it; subtract it from the edge beam where they meet. 5) Show the 2D layout and BOM for review, then model it as one assembly (slab floor, recess floor, edge as Structural Foundation DirectShape, bolts, stub-ups) and clash-check it against the wall assemblies: bolts through bottom plates are intended. 6) Re-derive the anchors whenever a wall panel is rebuilt.
validation: Anchor report per plate segment: count, max gap, end distances, min distance to a stud axis
Stub-ups outside the thickened edge (except where intended)
Clash check against wall assemblies: only bolt x bottom plate / insulation
Placeholder host dependents checked before deletion
